extracted.intended_audience: Californians, utility stakeholders, journalists, and regulated entities (PG&E)
extracted.subtask_description: A California Public Utilities Commission press release announcing and describing the terms of a settlement/penalty and related enforcement actions taken against a regulated utility (PG&E) for wildfire- and safety-related violations. It summarizes the settlement terms, required corrective actions, and historical enforcement context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total settlement penalty amount
rubrics_metrics.description: PG&E will pay a $45 million penalty for its involvement in the 2021 Dixie Fire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the headline monetary penalty imposed by the settlement agreement approved by the CPUC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shareholder-funded capital expenditures for electronic records initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: $40 million in shareholder funding for capital expenditures for an initiative to transition from hard copy records to electronic records for distribution patrols and inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds must be used to implement a records modernization project intended to improve recording accuracy and enable more timely inspections and preventive maintenance. PG&E must submit a detailed implementation plan to SED, which can be modified, and must provide annual reports for oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fines to the California General Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: $2.5 million in fines to the California General Fund as part of the settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary component of the settlement allocated directly to the state general fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal remediation payments
rubrics_metrics.description: $2.5 million in payments to tribes impacted by the Dixie Fire for remediations (to be distributed to the Greenville Rancheria and Maidu Summitt Consortium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement includes directed remediation funding to specified tribal and tribal-affiliated organizations; PG&E is responsible for distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation plan submission and SED oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the settlement, PG&E will submit an implementation plan to SED detailing the project design for the new record-keeping initiative; SED has the right to modify the plan and PG&E will submit annual reports to SED for ongoing oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a concrete project design, allows regulator modification, and mandates periodic (annual) reporting to verify progress and compliance. This is an ongoing compliance/monitoring requirement, not a one-time payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and expected safety benefits of the record-keeping initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: The initiative will support public safety by enabling more accurate recording of information and immediate awareness of the condition of PG&E’s assets, thereby improving timeliness of inspections and preventive maintenance, and assisting the CPUC in conducting future audits and investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the safety rationale and outcome measures the CPUC expects from the funded project (accuracy, timeliness, inspection effectiveness, auditability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Administrative Consent Order (ACO) as an enforcement tool
rubrics_metrics.description: The settlement agreement followed SED’s investigation and issuance of an Administrative Consent Order (ACO). The ACO is one of many enforcement tools included in the CPUC’s Enforcement Policy (established 2020) to allow streamlined enforcement actions in lieu of issuing citations or seeking a formal Order Instituting Investigation (OII).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes procedural enforcement option: ACOs are intended as a streamlined alternative to more formal proceedings and align CPUC practice with many other state and local enforcement agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined enforcement practice alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Addition of ACOs and other tools moved the CPUC’s practices more in-line with the enforcement practices of many other state and local enforcement agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy rationale for using a broader toolkit for enforcement; implies a standard that enforcement may be pursued through less-formal but binding settlement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of violations and enforcement actions CPUC pursues (historical examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: CPUC has penalized PG&E for multiple wildfire- and safety-related incidents (e.g., Zogg Fire, Brewer Fire, Easy Fire, Kincade Fire) and for failures such as inadequate inspections, guideline violations during PSPS events, and failure to prioritize vegetation clearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of past penalties and citations illustrates the categories of conduct that trigger enforcement: wildfire ignition causation, safety violations during specific incidents, inspection lapses, noncompliance with PSPS guidance, and vegetation management failures. These examples serve as precedent and guidance for enforcement priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement for inspection and maintenance deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: CPUC issued a $5 million citation for failure to thoroughly inspect specific transmission lines (Ignacio-Alto-Sausalito) from 2009–2018 and a $2.5 million citation for incomplete distribution pole inspections in 2019 that violated CPUC regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulator enforces statutory/regulatory inspection requirements; failure to meet inspection obligations can result in citations and monetary penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective directives and incident-specific remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: CPUC issued directives requiring corrective actions (e.g., regarding an incident with a Cellon-treated pole in Danville, Calif. in 2020) and other incident-specific measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond fines, CPUC can order specific remedial actions tailored to the incident to correct practices and prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancement of Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) processes
rubrics_metrics.description: CPUC ordered PG&E to enhance its Public Safety Power Shutoff process and issued an ALJ decision penalizing PG&E for violating guidelines during Fall 2019 PSPS events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory expectation that utilities maintain, follow, and improve PSPS procedures; failure to adhere to PSPS guidelines can result in penalties and orders to enhance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer reporting tools requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: CPUC ordered PG&E to create a mobile app for customers to report electric infrastructure safety concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory direction to improve channels for customer-sourced safety reporting, increasing transparency and responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of safety performance metrics and Enhanced Oversight/Enforcement Process
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPUC established specific metrics to systemically evaluate PG&E’s operational safety performance and to implement the Enhanced Oversight and Enforcement Process imposed upon PG&E as a condition of approving PG&E’s bankruptcy exit plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulator sets measurable performance metrics and a formal oversight process that condition ongoing regulatory relief; these metrics inform evaluation, escalation, and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and escalation within Enhanced Oversight based on vegetation management failures
rubrics_metrics.description: CPUC placed PG&E into the first step of the Enhanced Oversight and Enforcement Process based on the company’s failure to sufficiently prioritize clearing vegetation on its highest-risk power lines as part of its wildfire mitigation work in 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an example of the trigger for escalation: failure to meet vegetation management expectations can lead to formal entry into an enhanced oversight regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate mitigation directives for operational programs (Fast Trip example)
rubrics_metrics.description: CPUC directed PG&E to take immediate action to reduce and mitigate customer impacts from the sudden loss of power due to PG&E’s execution of its Fast Trip program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulator can mandate prompt operational changes and mitigations when utility programs cause unacceptable customer impacts or safety risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and expectations for an Independent Safety Monitor
rubrics_metrics.description: CPUC established standards, scope, and expectations for an Independent Safety Monitor overseeing PG&E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent oversight can be codified with defined standards and scope as part of enforcement and monitoring to ensure compliance with safety obligations.
